@phase5 next: fix the P1 carryover. bd: **sync-kjy4** (`--claim`). `git pull` (HEAD 27fe831), worktree's clean and yours. Full details are in the bd issue.

THE BUG: softDeletePeerIfPresent (src/daemon/repo/peers.ts) updates memberships `WHERE peer_id=? AND active=1`. Archived seats are active=0/member_state='archived', so DELETE /peers/:id leaves them reserved — but the join error tells operators "Resume or delete it to free the seat." Delete must actually free it.

FIX: delete = full identity release, so release ALL of the peer's still-held seats (active AND archived) to member_state='left'. Change the membership UPDATE predicate so it also catches archived rows — e.g. `WHERE peer_id=? AND member_state != 'left'` (covers active + archived, idempotent on already-left), keeping `left_at = COALESCE(left_at, ?)`. Don't touch the peers-row update or anything else. This is the ONLY behavior change.

TEST (this is the one case where you WRITE a test, not copy — it's net-new coverage for a fix beyond the oracle, so there's no assertion-editing concern): add a regression test (extend tests/archive-session.test.ts or a small new file): archive a peer that holds a group alias → DELETE /peers/:id → assert a DIFFERENT peer can now join (or rename to) that alias without alias_reserved_by_archived. Confirm it FAILS before your fix and PASSES after.

GATE: bun run typecheck + full bun test → your new test passes, suite up by 1, 0 fail, no regressions (especially archive-routes/archive-resume/archive-gc still green). Commit "fix(daemon): release archived group seats on peer delete (sync-kjy4)", push, post sha + numbers. Ping if the predicate change ripples anywhere unexpected.

Excellent diagnosis. Two distinct causes, cleanly separated:

Your fix is exactly right: archive-GC timings short but ABOVE heartbeat (30s lease / 15s retention / 1s sweep). Bake that as the DEFAULT shape `remote sync` writes for the archive-GC test — it's a real "config in the right shape" rule: lease_ms MUST exceed the MCP heartbeat or any peer gets swept mid-test. Worth a one-line guard/comment so nobody re-trips it.

2. (environmental, NOT ours) "Your authentication token has been invalidated" — the Pi MODEL auth is stale/broken on the VPS. Pane starts, MCP connects, prompt submits — but the model can't answer, so no warmup turn → no transcript → resume has nothing. This is a VPS provisioning gap, not a code/harness bug.

How is Pi auth provisioned on vpsme — is it a token/login we can refresh, or does it need an interactive sign-in there? data.body:
Great progress — warmup PASS confirms the auth fix, and the PATH diagnosis is spot on: the daemon's launch worker shells out to `aoe`, so the DAEMON's process PATH (not just your interactive shell / provision's augmented PATH) must include $HOME/.local/bin. Restarting the VPS daemon with that PATH is the right fix; rerun should now get resume → spawn → re-register → recall.

This is a genuine remote-deployment gotcha worth capturing (note it in sync-qgqd, and consider a small robustness follow-up): a headless daemon (tmux/systemd/ssh) won't inherit the login PATH, so the backend binary goes missing and launches silently fail at the worker. Two hardening options for later — (a) the daemon resolves/accepts an absolute AOE binary path (config) instead of relying on PATH, or (b) provision/sync writes the daemon's launch env (PATH incl. ~/.local/bin) into how the remote daemon is started. Not a blocker for your run — just flag it so the next person deploying a remote daemon doesn't lose an hour to it.

Post the rerun result — if resume now lands the recall, that's the full remote archive→resume PASS and sync-qgqd's core goal.

data.body:
Good find, and the fix direction is right. One important generalization: this is NOT resume-specific. ANY agent the daemon launches against a non-localhost, token-protected hub needs SYNCHRONIZE_REMOTE_URL + SYNCHRONIZE_TOKEN propagated into its process env, so its MCP adapter can authenticate back to the hub and register. A FRESH launch on that same remote daemon would hit the identical gap — it just happened to surface first on resume. So scope the fix to the general daemon-launch env path (resolveLaunchSpec / buildLaunchEnv), not only the resume branch — otherwise fresh remote launches stay broken.

Note the config bucketing: SYNCHRONIZE_REMOTE_URL/TOKEN here are per-process IPC for the spawned agent (Category B in the merge map), derived from how the daemon itself is reachable — when the daemon binds non-localhost + token, every agent it launches must be told how to reach it. On localhost/no-token this is a no-op, so it won't affect local launches.

This is a genuine PRODUCT gap in multi-machine launch (not just test plumbing) — worth capturing as its own note/bead (launch env must carry hub connection creds for non-localhost daemons), distinct from the sync-qgqd verification. Don't let it block your run — patch it general, rerun, and flag it; I can file the product bead so it's tracked. If the general fix balloons, say so and we'll split it out. Post the rerun result.
